query: What are the main AI techniques used for early autism diagnosis?
summary:
Artificial intelligence (AI) techniques used for early autism diagnosis include machine learning (ML) models, deep learning (DL), and artificial neural networks (ANNs) [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 1, 2, 3].

Specific techniques mentioned are:
*   **Multiclass decision forest algorithm**: Employed by Choi et al. to classify children with different neurodevelopmental conditions, including ASD and PDD-NOS, using ADI-R test data [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 11].
*   **Artificial Neural Network (ANN)**: Used by Abdulhay et al. for classifying ASD from neurotypical children based on resting-state EEG data [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 11]. ANNs have also been used for classifying 3D kinematic gait features and raw motion data from a drag and drop task [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   **Support Vector Machines (SVMs)**: Demonstrated good accuracy in diagnosing ASD and used to identify microbial predictors from microbiome composition [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 2, 7].
*   **k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)**: Also shown to have good accuracy in ASD diagnosis [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 2].
*   **Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)**: Applied to facial images for early stage detection of ASD [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   **Random Forest (RF)**: Used with eye-tracking data to identify distinct eye movement patterns, with metagenomic sequencing data of gut microbiota, and with microbiome composition [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   **Multilayer Perceptron (MLP)**: Used with facial images for early stage detection [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   **Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM)**: Applied to facial images for early stage detection [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   **AdaBoost (AB)**: Used with facial images for early stage detection [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   **Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT)**: Employed to predict behavioral traits in individuals with ASD through text-based data analysis [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   **EKNN (hybrid combining KNN, NB, and COA)**: Used with blood tests to enhance accuracy and speed in detection [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].

These techniques analyze various data modalities, including visual (facial, home videos, eye-tracking), motor function, behavioral, microbiome, genetic, and neuroimaging data [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 1].

**Key findings:**
*   AI models show promise in reducing human error and improving diagnostic accuracy in ASD research [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 2].
*   ML models can analyze complex datasets to identify key features associated with ASD [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 2].
*   AI-driven approaches have demonstrated high accuracy in classifying ASD using diverse data types [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 1].

**Numerical data (with sources):**
*   Choi et al.'s decision forest model achieved an accuracy of **81%** in predicting PDD-NOS when using 4 or 8 decision trees [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 11].
*   Abdulhay et al.'s ANN classification method achieved an overall accuracy of **95.90%**, with a sensitivity of **96.72%** and specificity of **95.08%**, using resting-state EEG data [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 11].
*   Meng et al., 2023, used RF with eye-tracking data, achieving **73%** accuracy [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   Rabbi et al., 2021, used CNN with facial images, achieving **92.31%** accuracy; MLP achieved **71.66%**; RF achieved **72.78%**; GBM achieved **75.23%**; AB achieved **74.56%** [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   Hasan et al., 2017, used ANN with 3D kinematic gait features, achieving **88.3%** (Kinematic-Raw), **90.0%** (Kinematic-TMWU), and **91.7%** (Kinematic-SWDA) accuracy [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   Lu and Perkowski, 2021, used CNN (VGG16) with 2D facial images, achieving **95%** accuracy [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   Pal and Rubini, 2024, used BERT with TASD Dataset Behavioral Traits and Features, achieving **88%** accuracy [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   Luongo et al., 2024, used ANN with raw motion data, achieving **90%** accuracy (2 features) and **76%** (4 features) [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   Wang and Fu, 2023, used RF with metagenomic sequencing data of gut microbiota, achieving **67%** (Moscow cohort), **97%** (Shenzhen cohort), and **80%** (combined) accuracy [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   Rabie and Saleh, 2023, used EKNN with blood tests, achieving **93%** accuracy [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].
*   Olaguez-Gonzalez et al., 2023, used SVM with microbiome composition, achieving **90%** accuracy; ANN achieved **80%**; RF achieved **90%** [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 7].

**Risk flags (if any):**
*   Challenges remain related to data quality, privacy, ethics, and clinical integration of AI tools [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 1].
*   Reliance on behavioral observation data can be subjective and prone to inconsistencies [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 3].
*   Further research is needed to refine AI models and ensure their validity and reliability in clinical settings, especially for behavioral assessments [source: The Role of Artificial Intelligence for Early Diagnostic Tools of Autism.pdf.pdf, page 3].

**Confidence level:**
5/5
